summary.headline: DCW Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell 28% YoY to INR41.4 crore as PVC losses (West Asia VCM shortage, duty suspension) hit Basic Chemicals to a negative INR14 crore EBITDA.
summary.overview: Revenue rose 14% YoY to INR542 crore, led by Specialty Chemicals (INR177 crore, 33% of revenue, up 38% YoY), but fell 11% QoQ on a one-time Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation base effect. Consolidated EBITDA including other income was INR41.4 crore, down 28% YoY and 41% QoQ, with management attributing the drop mainly to PVC disruption. Basic Chemicals EBITDA was negative INR14 crore, while Specialty EBITDA grew about 20% YoY. Management guided that PVC conditions have improved since Q1 and that FY27 should close better than FY26, while also announcing a INR250 crore capex programme and an intent to be effectively net debt free by end-FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY (as stated in opening remarks); +6% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; margin 29.1% (analyst-computed from Q1 FY26 33.6%)
Negative INR14 crore (-5.2% margin per analyst)

financial_highlights.change: from migration to new tax regime (25.17% vs 34.9%)

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (CPVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR177 crore, up 38% YoY with CPVC volumes up 59% and SIOP volumes up about 3%. EBITDA grew about 20% YoY and 35% QoQ; margin about 29% vs 33.6% a year ago, which management linked to PVC-CPVC spread volatility.

segments.name: Basic Chemicals (PVC, caustic soda, soda ash, Synthetic Rutile)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore, down 18% QoQ on Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation. EBITDA negative INR14 crore; management estimated a sequential PVC contribution swing of INR50-55 crore, with caustic soda and Synthetic Rutile margins improving.

guidance_outlook: FY27 expected to close at a better level than FY26, based on current visibility (management).
Basic Chemicals expected to do better than Q1; management says breakeven in Q2 is more than believed if normalcy holds.
Steady-state EBITDA assessed at about INR300 crore, replacing the earlier INR400 crore target.
Legacy long-term debt expected to be fully repaid in FY27 (repayments about INR135 crore); effectively net debt free by end-FY27 before new borrowings.
Targeting minimum incremental ROCE of 20% on new investments.
Expects to borrow slightly more than repayments for the capex, with a 1-1.5% negative carry on cash-to-borrowing.
capex_capacity: INR250 crore programme over 2-3 years; first part is SIOP capacity expansion from about 30,000 tpa to 45,000 tpa, with Phase 1 adding 7,000 tpa by Q4 FY28 and infrastructure sized for a further 8,000 tpa.
Captive power infrastructure at Sahupuram facility, targeted for Q4 FY28, to lower power costs across Specialty and Basic Chemicals.
SIOP expansion is brownfield; expected margin around 35-36% and product price north of INR80,000/ton (management).
Current PVC capacity about 1 lakh tpa; CPVC about 50,000 tpa; SIOP capacity 28 kt fully tied up this year after debottlenecking.
Synthetic Rutile capacity about 48,000-50,000 tpa; caustic soda realistic capacity about 90,000 tpa.
demand_pricing: PVC: West Asia conflict cut VCM availability from traditional Asian suppliers, forcing spot purchases from China at higher prices; import duty suspension let in lower-priced imports. Duties now reinstated and a minimum import price (MIP, about USD/INR80 per ton equivalent) introduced for suspension-grade PVC.
Management said current import parity is about USD820-860/ton, well above MIP, and expects prices to stay at these levels at least this quarter.
PVC/VCM spread was estimated at north of INR25,000/ton; PVC-to-CPVC spread lags because of existing customer orders.
Synthetic Rutile: prices recovered vs last year's inventory-correction slump; customer mix improved and high-priced deliveries are back-ended.

SIOP: around 60% of output exported, mainly to the US; management says no tariff impact on exports. Volumes are seasonally higher in Q3 and Q4. Ammonia cost increases were passed through to customers.
Caustic soda margins expanded QoQ and YoY; chlorine is now fully consumed captively for CPVC, improving caustic ECU realisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the QoQ revenue decline came from captive PVC use, lower PVC output and the Synthetic Rutile base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 Synthetic Rutile liquidation base effect was the main driver, plus a few days of PVC plant shutdown; it did not quantify the split, but said the Synthetic Rutile effect alone would have exceeded the top-line decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Specialty margins compress and is about 29% the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins depend on the dynamic PVC-CPVC spread, which is volatile. SIOP margins are robust, and a steady-state margin is hard to pin down because roughly 40-50% of PVC goes into CPVC.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Basic Chemicals' loss came from PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only a directional estimate: a sequential contribution swing of INR50-55 crore in PVC. It confirmed PVC was the only loss-making Basic Chemicals product, with caustic soda, soda ash and Synthetic Rutile profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR400 crore EBITDA target still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It was set when CPVC margins were about 40%. Management now sees steady-state EBITDA of about INR300 crore, subject to the spread holding.

qa_highlights.question: Would a share buyback be considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still considering a buyback and will announce it at an opportune time if it decides to proceed.

qa_highlights.question: How is VCM sourced, and can it be derisked or backward integrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply moved from a single Qatar producer to a global distributor sourcing across Asia. Management ruled out backward integration at current scale; storage expansion would add only about 10-15 days of inventory.

risks_watch: Whether VCM supply from the global distributor and import parity (about USD820-860/ton) hold through the quarter, and whether PVC prices stay clear of the MIP level.
PVC-to-CPVC spread lag: management flagged that old customer orders priced at lower spreads will weigh on Specialty margins as PVC prices rise.
Basic Chemicals breakeven in Q2 FY27 depends on the situation staying normal; management said July still carried stock bought at high VCM costs.

Execution and funding of the INR250 crore capex: SIOP Phase 1 (7,000 tpa) and Sahupuram captive power both targeted for Q4 FY28; borrowing slightly above repayments of about INR135 crore, with negative carry of 1-1.5%.
Revised steady-state EBITDA of about INR300 crore versus the earlier INR400 crore target; management did not give a timeline for reaching it.
Possible share buyback: management said it is still considering it, with no decision or timing announced.
key_quotes: Importantly, we see these pressures as largely event-driven rather than structural.
Despite the impact of PVC in quarter 1, based on current visibility, we continue to expect FY27 to close at a better level than the previous fiscal.
So we can only give you a directional number because the fixed cost allocation for the basic chemicals are common.
We more than believe if the situation stays as normalcy as it is today.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about a difficult PVC quarter, attributing it to external and largely one-time factors (West Asia VCM shortage, duty suspension), and was confident on recovery in Basic Chemicals and FY27. It was cautious and evasive on steady-state Specialty margins, PVC-CPVC spread, the buyback and the segment-level PVC loss, giving directional or no numbers where pressed.

adds.what: SIOP capacity expansion from ~30,000 tpa to 45,000 tpa; Phase 1 adds 7,000 tpa (part of INR250 crore programme)
Captive power infrastructure at Sahupuram facility to lower power costs

growth.why: Management expects FY27 to close better than FY26 and Basic Chemicals to improve toward Q2 breakeven, but Q1 EBITDA fell 28% YoY to INR41.4 crore on PVC disruption, PVC volumes are down 20%, and the SIOP expansion (30kt to 45kt, Phase 1 +7kt) only comes online by Q4 FY28.
